q: Sheffield Wednesday took their unusual name from what?
o: The day of the week their cricket club played
The date of their first match
hint: The club began in 1867 as the football section of The Wednesday Cricket Club, whose members played on their half-day off.

q: By what nickname are Sheffield Wednesday known?
hint: It comes from Owlerton, the district they moved to in 1899, and an owl has been on the badge ever since.

q: Which stadium has been Sheffield Wednesday's home since 1899?
hint: The ground took its name from the surrounding district of Hillsborough in north Sheffield.

q: Sheffield Wednesday's fierce rivalry, the Steel City derby, is with which club?
hint: The two Sheffield clubs have contested the fixture since the 1890s, and it takes its name from the city's steel industry.

q: How many English league titles have Sheffield Wednesday won?
hint: They came in 1903, 1904, 1929 and 1930 — two pairs of back-to-back championships, three decades apart.

q: Sheffield Wednesday won the League Cup in 1991 by beating which club in the final?
hint: Wednesday were a Second Division side at the time, making it a considerable upset at Wembley.

q: Who scored Sheffield Wednesday's winning goal in the 1991 League Cup final?
hint: Sheridan struck the only goal of the game; it remains the club's most recent major trophy.

q: Which manager led Sheffield Wednesday to the 1991 League Cup?
hint: Atkinson had managed the beaten finalists earlier in his career, which added an edge to the day.

q: In 1993 Sheffield Wednesday lost both domestic cup finals to which club?
hint: Arsenal beat them in the League Cup final and then again in an FA Cup final replay, a uniquely cruel season.

q: Which winger, famous for his time at Marseille and for England, joined Sheffield Wednesday in 1992?
hint: Waddle was voted the Football Writers' Footballer of the Year in his first season at Hillsborough.

q: How many FA Cups have Sheffield Wednesday won?
hint: The wins came in 1896, 1907 and 1935 — the last of them nearly a century ago.

q: Sheffield Wednesday were founded in 1867, making them one of the oldest what?
o: Professional football clubs in the world
hint: Only a handful of clubs anywhere can claim an older continuous football history.

q: Which England striker spent most of his career at Sheffield Wednesday in the 1990s?
hint: Hirst is remembered at Hillsborough for his power and for once striking the fastest recorded shot in English football.

q: Which England defender, known for playing without shin pads, joined Sheffield Wednesday in 1993?
hint: Walker arrived from Sampdoria after a celebrated spell at Nottingham Forest and stayed for a decade.

q: What colours do Sheffield Wednesday traditionally wear at home?
hint: The blue and white stripes have been worn since the 1870s and distinguish them from their red-and-white city rivals.
